subject: Trying to use facet_grid() to introduce breaks in x axis

messages.author: 43b6c2f7e9e0e9b0
messages.subject: Trying to use facet_grid() to introduce breaks in x axis
parts:
Hello,

I have been trying to use facet_grid() to introduce breaks in x axis and ran a few problems. The example below tries to plot the Theoph data in three panels:
  • The left panel contains x between 0 and 5
  • The middle panel contains x between 10 and 13
  • The right panel contains x between 23 and 25.
I would like the panel widths to be proportional to the x ranges (5:3:2 ratio) and each panel shows the entire range (rather than just the parts where data exist), so that the x ticks will have the same width. Is there a way to control this in ggplot2? I tried to do this with manually arranging viewports, but I quickly learned that it would be great to take advantage of what ggplot2 already does well with facets, e.g. to deal with legends. If you can point me to ggplot2 functions I have to look into to make this happen, that will be very helpful.

Thank you very much.

Sincerely,
Junghoon 

library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)
  
# Specify the x ranges to plot in each panel:
rangeList <- list(c(0, 5), c(10, 13), c(23, 25))
 
# Identify panels:
dataArray <- transform(Theoph, 
                       panel = NA)
for (iRange in 1:length(rangeList)) {
  dataArray[rangeList[[iRange]][1] <= dataArray$Time &
              dataArray$Time <= rangeList[[iRange]][2], "panel"] <- iRange
} # for
dataArray <- dataArray[!is.na(dataArray$panel), ]
 
# Create plot:
obj <- ggplot(dataArray, aes(x = Time, y = conc, color = Subject)) + 
  geom_point(size = 4)
print(obj + 
        facet_grid(. ~ panel, scale = "free_x") + 
        theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
              strip.text = element_blank()))

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Trying to use facet_grid() to introduce breaks in x axis
parts:
Junghoon, you probably want to look at the "space" option of facet_grid? For example

# a reproducible example -- hint, hint!
df <- data.frame(panel=c(1,1,2,2,2,3,3),x=1:7,y=runif(7))  
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y))+geom_point()
p <- p + facet_grid(~panel, scales="free", space="free")
p <- p + scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:7, expand=c(0, 0.5))
print(p)

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Trying to use facet_grid() to introduce breaks in x axis
parts:
Not as far as I know, except for the 'expand' parameter to scale_x_continuous above (but that will affect all the facets). If you want to expand one particular panel's x limits, I don't have a better suggestion than your transparent points idea. But maybe someone else will...

Regards,
Ben
